players.product: solder balls and micro solder balls (<130 µm) for BGA / CSP semiconductor packaging

quarterly_data.signal: 2Q 2026 IR deck: consolidated Q2 revenue KRW 908 hundred-million (YoY +58%), operating profit KRW 101 hundred-million (YoY +291%), OPM 11.1% (+6.6%pt); H1 revenue KRW 1,595 hundred-million (YoY +57%), described as record results. Drivers per the company: solder-ball (SB) price increases have taken hold, with a larger share of LME-linked pricing and volume growth across all customer groups even after the price rise; micro solder ball (MSB) margins stepped up and were the largest profit contributor, helped by a higher mix of high-margin fine balls and strong demand for HDDs going into AI data centers; paste & flux turned profitable on record volume and new powder sales. Watch items: SB material-cost ratio rose on a bigger mix of large balls (managed through price linkage), and inventory and receivables rose with advance raw-material purchases and sales growth. Separate (solder) 1Q26 revenue KRW 426 hundred-million (+63% YoY): SB 254 (+82%), MSB + CSB 104 (+63%), paste & flux and other 68 (+17%); 1Q26 operating profit KRW 23 hundred-million; quarterly separate revenue rose from 232 (1Q24) to 426 (1Q26), a record for four straight quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue KRW 908 hundred-million (+58% YoY); Q2 operating profit KRW 101 hundred-million (+291%); 1Q26 SB revenue 254 (+82%), MSB + CSB 104 (+63%)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and positioning per the deck: solder-ball capacity (SB + MSB + CSB) is about 2 billion K per month, and SB and cored-solder-ball (CSB) lines are being expanded; the company produces balls down to 30um with its in-house pulsated atomization process (PAP). It claims about 70% of the Korean SB market and a global top-tier / leading MSB position alongside a Japanese S company, with MSB (150um or below) used in FC-BGA for AI accelerators, ASICs and CPUs and in HDD recording heads; its key domestic S customer is running at full capacity and it is pursuing new MSB customers in Japan and China.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity about 2 billion K per month (SB + MSB + CSB); Korean SB share about 70%

quarterly_data.signal: Cored solder balls (Cu core, for mobile AP packaging such as FC-PoP and 2.5D packages, mass-produced for a single global A company) are in a new-product transition: revenue dipped temporarily as the main model was replaced, mass production of the new product has started and the ramp is to be in full swing in the second half of 2026; the company is sampling SB, MSB and CSB with major new customers to reduce single-customer dependence in CSB.
quarterly_data.figure: CSB new-product mass production started; full ramp in H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Customers per the deck: solder balls go to Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Amkor and others (Korean IDMs / OSATs plus global OSATs); MSB and CSB go to global OSATs; paste & flux to a domestic S company and other SMT customers. The top five customers were about 54.9% of 1Q26 revenue (about 55%). Paste & flux is currently mainly a low-margin Type 4/5 line for IT products; the company is developing higher-value Type 6/7 powders in response to customers' localization demand and has raised paste prices.
quarterly_data.figure: top five customers about 54.9% of 1Q26 revenue
